SG-02: Page metadata Status: ACTIVE (version 2) Category: Structure Every team website MUST set the following metadata in the document head. ## Title The page title MUST have the format: Team | Agentic SE Lab Example: `Team Null Pointers | Agentic SE Lab`. Use a vertical bar, not a dash. The group name in the title MUST match the group name shown in the page header. ## Language The root `` element MUST declare English as the page language: `lang="en"`. Even if some content is written in German, the declared language stays English. ## Other metadata - The character set MUST be UTF-8. - A `` tag MUST be present, see the responsive documents. - A `` SHOULD contain one sentence about the team. --- SG-58: Review checklist Status: ACTIVE Category: Meta Before submitting, go through this list: - [ ] Title and language set as described in the metadata document - [ ] Current day and night palettes used (not the deprecated ones) - [ ] Accent color defined as a custom property - [ ] Theme switching and persistence implemented as described in the theming documents - [ ] Toggle is an accessible button - [ ] One member card per member, each with a hot take badge - [ ] Photos have alt texts - [ ] Required sections with the correct ids - [ ] Exactly one h1 - [ ] Current footer text - [ ] Current breakpoint - [ ] System font, rem font sizes - [ ] Reduced motion respected --- SG-50: Responsive breakpoints (version 2) Status: ACTIVE (version 2) Category: Responsive Team websites use exactly one layout breakpoint. - The breakpoint MUST be written as `@media (max-width: 700px)`. The earlier, smaller breakpoint made cards too narrow on large phones. - Below the breakpoint: - member cards are shown in one column - the header content is stacked vertically - side padding is reduced to 1rem - The page MUST include ``. - Test your page at 375 px and 1280 px width. SG-22: Theme toggle control
Status: ACTIVE
Category: Theming

- The toggle MUST be a `<button>` element with the id `theme-toggle`.
- It MUST have an `aria-label` describing the action, for example `aria-label="Switch to night mode"`.
  Update the label when the theme changes.
- It SHOULD show a sun symbol in night mode and a moon symbol in day mode.
- It SHOULD be placed in the top right corner of the header.
- Don't use a checkbox for the toggle.

---

SG-20: Theme switching mechanics
Status: ACTIVE
Category: Theming

The theme is controlled by one attribute on the root element.

- The `<html>` element MUST carry the attribute `data-theme` with the value `light` or `dark`.
- JavaScript switches the theme by changing this attribute, not by toggling classes on the body.
- The CSS MUST define the colors for each theme with attribute selectors, for example
  `[data-theme="light"] { ... }` and `[data-theme="dark"] { ... }`.
- Components use CSS custom properties (for example `var(--bg)`), so they don't need theme-specific rules.

---

SG-21: Theme persistence (version 2)
Status: ACTIVE (version 2)
Category: Theming

The theme choice of the user is remembered between visits.

- The choice MUST be stored in `localStorage` under the key `upb-theme`.
  The old key was too generic and collided with other local files.
- The stored value is either `light` or `dark`.
- On page load, read the stored value. If there is none, follow the operating system preference.
- Apply the theme as early as possible to avoid a flash of the wrong theme.

---

SG-18: Dark mode philosophy
Status: ACTIVE
Category: Theming

Users choose their theme, but we start with a sensible default.

- If the user has never chosen a theme, the page SHOULD follow the operating system preference (`prefers-color-scheme`).
- As soon as the user clicks the toggle, their choice wins and is remembered, see the theme persistence document.
- Switching the theme MUST NOT reload the page.

SG-20: Theme switching mechanics
Status: ACTIVE
Category: Theming

The theme is controlled by one attribute on the root element.

- The `<html>` element MUST carry the attribute `data-theme` with the value `light` or `dark`.
- JavaScript switches the theme by changing this attribute, not by toggling classes on the body.
- The CSS MUST define the colors for each theme with attribute selectors, for example
  `[data-theme="light"] { ... }` and `[data-theme="dark"] { ... }`.
- Components use CSS custom properties (for example `var(--bg)`), so they don't need theme-specific rules.

Status: ACTIVE (version 2)
Category: Theming

The theme choice of the user is remembered between visits.

- The stored value is either `light` or `dark`.
- On page load, read the stored value. If there is none, follow the operating system preference.
- Apply the theme as early as possible to avoid a flash of the wrong theme.

SG-18: Dark mode philosophy
Status: ACTIVE
Category: Theming

Users choose their theme, but we start with a sensible default.

- If the user has never chosen a theme, the page SHOULD follow the operating system preference (`prefers-color-scheme`).
- As soon as the user clicks the toggle, their choice wins and is remembered, see the theme persistence document.
- Switching the theme MUST NOT reload the page.

Status: ACTIVE
Category: Theming

The theme is controlled by one attribute on the root element.

Status: ACTIVE
Category: Theming

The theme is controlled by one attribute on the root element.

- The CSS MUST define the colors for each theme with attribute selectors, for example
  `[data-theme="light"] { ... }` and `[data-theme="dark"] { ... }`.

SG-22: Theme toggle control
Status: ACTIVE
Category: Theming

- The toggle MUST be a `<button>` element with the id `theme-toggle`.
- It MUST have an `aria-label` describing the action, for example `aria-label="Switch to night mode"`.
  Update the label when the theme changes.
- It SHOULD show a sun symbol in night mode and a moon symbol in day mode.
- It SHOULD be placed in the top right corner of the header.
- Don't use a checkbox for the toggle.

---

SG-20: Theme switching mechanics
Status: ACTIVE
Category: Theming

The theme is controlled by one attribute on the root element.

- The `<html>` element MUST carry the attribute `data-theme` with the value `light` or `dark`.
- JavaScript switches the theme by changing this attribute, not by toggling classes on the body.
- The CSS MUST define the colors for each theme with attribute selectors, for example
  `[data-theme="light"] { ... }` and `[data-theme="dark"] { ... }`.
- Components use CSS custom properties (for example `var(--bg)`), so they don't need theme-specific rules.

---

SG-21: Theme persistence (version 2)
Status: ACTIVE (version 2)
Category: Theming

The theme choice of the user is remembered between visits.

- The choice MUST be stored in `localStorage` under the key `upb-theme`.
  The old key was too generic and collided with other local files.
- The stored value is either `light` or `dark`.
- On page load, read the stored value. If there is none, follow the operating system preference.
- Apply the theme as early as possible to avoid a flash of the wrong theme.

---

SG-18: Dark mode philosophy
Status: ACTIVE
Category: Theming

Users choose their theme, but we start with a sensible default.

- If the user has never chosen a theme, the page SHOULD follow the operating system preference (`prefers-color-scheme`).
- As soon as the user clicks the toggle, their choice wins and is remembered, see the theme persistence document.
- Switching the theme MUST NOT reload the page.

SG-20: Theme switching mechanics
Status: ACTIVE
Category: Theming

The theme is controlled by one attribute on the root element.

- The `<html>` element MUST carry the attribute `data-theme` with the value `light` or `dark`.

- The CSS MUST define the colors for each theme with attribute selectors, for example
  `[data-theme="light"] { ... }` and `[data-theme="dark"] { ... }`.
- Components use CSS custom properties (for example `var(--bg)`), so they don't need theme-specific rules.

Status: ACTIVE
Category: Theming

SG-22: Theme toggle control
Status: ACTIVE
Category: Theming

- The toggle MUST be a `<button>` element with the id `theme-toggle`.
- It MUST have an `aria-label` describing the action, for example `aria-label="Switch to night mode"`.
  Update the label when the theme changes.
- It SHOULD show a sun symbol in night mode and a moon symbol in day mode.
- It SHOULD be placed in the top right corner of the header.
- Don't use a checkbox for the toggle.

SG-20: Theme switching mechanics
Status: ACTIVE
Category: Theming

The theme is controlled by one attribute on the root element.

- The `<html>` element MUST carry the attribute `data-theme` with the value `light` or `dark`.
- JavaScript switches the theme by changing this attribute, not by toggling classes on the body.
- The CSS MUST define the colors for each theme with attribute selectors, for example
  `[data-theme="light"] { ... }` and `[data-theme="dark"] { ... }`.
- Components use CSS custom properties (for example `var(--bg)`), so they don't need theme-specific rules.

---

SG-21: Theme persistence (version 2)
Status: ACTIVE (version 2)
Category: Theming

The theme choice of the user is remembered between visits.

- The choice MUST be stored in `localStorage` under the key `upb-theme`.
  The old key was too generic and collided with other local files.
- The stored value is either `light` or `dark`.
- On page load, read the stored value. If there is none, follow the operating system preference.
- Apply the theme as early as possible to avoid a flash of the wrong theme.

---

SG-18: Dark mode philosophy
Status: ACTIVE
Category: Theming

Users choose their theme, but we start with a sensible default.

- If the user has never chosen a theme, the page SHOULD follow the operating system preference (`prefers-color-scheme`).
- As soon as the user clicks the toggle, their choice wins and is remembered, see the theme persistence document.
- Switching the theme MUST NOT reload the page.

- JavaScript switches the theme by changing this attribute, not by toggling classes on the body.
- The CSS MUST define the colors for each theme with attribute selectors, for example
  `[data-theme="light"] { ... }` and `[data-theme="dark"] { ... }`.
- Components use CSS custom properties (for example `var(--bg)`), so they don't need theme-specific rules.

SG-21: Theme persistence (version 2)
Status: ACTIVE (version 2)
Category: Theming

The theme choice of the user is remembered between visits.

- The choice MUST be stored in `localStorage` under the key `upb-theme`.
  The old key was too generic and collided with other local files.
- The stored value is either `light` or `dark`.
- On page load, read the stored value. If there is none, follow the operating system preference.
- Apply the theme as early as possible to avoid a flash of the wrong theme.
